Title: The Gate of Acheron, Constant Revolution, Smiling Jack and LSJ / Ankha ruling

Messages.Author: Kilrauko
Messages.Body:
1) As the wording in upcoming The Gate of Acheron is different and without X format of Constant revolution, does the card follow "all are discarded at once" ruling?

2) Or is the randomization determined per counter basis following the Smiling Jack procedure and ruling?

3) Is the wording intended to follow Smiling Jack?

Laying out the concern here: Acheron has 5 counters can the prey choose to discard 1R (shuffle graveyard, discard 1 at random pull), pay 1 pool, shuffle graveyard that was turned face up again to discard 1R, pay 1 pool, shuffle....Now think over 3 turns at first 3, 5 and 8 counters. Is it design intent to have 8 times the random pull from graveyard at the end with all the time it takes to sufficiently randomize (and the can of worms that opens) with ability to change between each pull as different cards are removed. As pointed out in the discord thread, this is relevant with all ash heap interaction and thus cannot be outright ruled to be 5.3. Slow Play yet it *will* take longer to handle compared to Constant Revolution which is one physical manipulation of the ash heap.

Below are the relevant tidbits and links, I'll type the upcoming card via edit once I get some morning tea in me.

Messages.Author: Ankha
Messages.Body:
> Kilrauko wrote:
> 1) As the wording in upcoming The Gate of Acheron is different and without X format of Constant revolution, does the card follow "all are discarded at once" ruling?
>
Yes, it works the same.

> Kilrauko wrote:
> 2) Or is the randomization determined per counter basis following the Smiling Jack procedure and ruling?
>
SJ works the same. You have to make the choice blood/pool in one go. For instance, you cannot burn the last blood on a vampire, interrupt the resolution of SJ by burning Jake Washington to give that vampire 4 blood, and proceed with burning newly gained blood from that vampire.

> Kilrauko wrote:
> 3) Is the wording intended to follow Smiling Jack?
>
They all work the same.
